Roofing Near Houston, Town by Town

Permit rules change at every city line, and part of the coast falls under the state windstorm program. Find your town, read its rules, and call one free number for a local roofer.

How coverage works across greater Houston

Searching for roofing near Houston turns up companies from all over the region. The line works the other way round: you call one number, say where you are, and the call goes to an independent roofing company that takes jobs in your area.

There is no office in any of these towns, no crew and no truck. Houston Expert Roofers answers the phone and passes the call on. The roofing company you reach decides whether it can come out and when, and it quotes and does the work.

The paperwork is the part that differs between towns. Some cities permit and inspect a re-roof, some only when the decking is replaced, and in unincorporated county areas a shingle replacement usually needs no permit at all. Along the coast, the state windstorm program adds an inspection of its own. Each town page below explains its own rules, with sources.

Harris County

The City of Houston, including Kingwood, permits re-roofs. Around it are smaller cities with their own rules and large unincorporated communities such as Cypress, Spring, Atascocita and Channelview, where Harris County does not permit an ordinary shingle replacement.

Coastal windstorm rules. In the Texas Department of Insurance's designated catastrophe area (Brazoria, Chambers, Galveston and the other first-tier coastal counties, plus, in Harris County, Morgan's Point and the parts of La Porte, Pasadena, Seabrook and Shoreacres inside city limits and east of State Highway 146), roof work must meet the windstorm building code and be inspected while it is under way. When it passes, TDI issues a certificate of compliance (form WPI-8), which the Texas Windstorm Insurance Association uses to decide whether it can insure the home. Ask the roofer, in writing, who schedules the inspection and when you will get the WPI-8.

What to ask, wherever you live

  • Is my address inside city limits, and does this job need a permit? Will you pull it in your name?
  • Is my home in the windstorm catastrophe area, and will you schedule the inspection and get me the WPI-8?
  • Does my HOA or deed restriction need to approve the shingle and color first?
  • Can you send me your certificate of liability insurance and a few addresses of roofs near me?

Texas has no state roofing license. No state agency licenses roofing contractors in Texas, and a 2025 bill to create one (HB 3344) did not reach a vote of the full House before the session ended. So check what you can: a certificate of liability insurance sent to you, a written contract with the full scope, a permit where your city requires one, local addresses you can drive past, and the shingle maker's warranty registration. Some cities also ask roofers to register. The line does not check any of this for you. How to check a roofer before you hire.

  1. Call the numberAn automated assistant answers (832) 662-4107 at any hour and asks which service you need, since the line also takes heating, cooling, pressure washing and water damage calls.
  2. Describe the roofA leak, missing shingles, hail, a limb on the roof or an old roof you want looked at, plus your part of greater Houston and how urgent it is.
  3. Get put throughYour call is transferred to an independent, locally owned roofing company, which hears a short summary before it picks up.
  4. Deal with the roofer directlyIt inspects, quotes and does the work, and you pay it (or your insurer does, as you arrange). If it misses the call, it gets your name, number, city and need to call you back.

Questions Houston homeowners ask

Does Houston Expert Roofers have an office in each town?

No. It has no offices, crews or trucks anywhere. It is a phone line that answers calls from across greater Houston and transfers each one to an independent roofing company that takes calls in that area. The town pages explain local rules so you know what to ask that company.

My town is not on the list. Can I still call?

Yes, as long as the address is in Montgomery, Harris, Galveston, Fort Bend, Chambers or Brazoria County. Towns get their own page when people there search for roofing often enough to show up in keyword data. Calls are not limited to those 28 towns. The line does not take calls for places outside greater Houston.

Why do roofing permit rules differ between Houston suburbs?

Each city writes its own permit rules, and unincorporated county areas usually have no residential permit for a shingle job at all. That is why a re-roof in Sugar Land or Kingwood (inside the City of Houston) is permitted and inspected, while the same job in much of Cypress or Spring is not. Ask the roofer which rule applies at your address and whether it will pull the permit.

Which greater Houston towns are in the Texas windstorm area?

The Texas Department of Insurance's catastrophe area covers all of Brazoria, Chambers and Galveston counties and, in Harris County, Morgan's Point plus the parts of La Porte, Pasadena, Seabrook and Shoreacres east of State Highway 146. Roof work there must pass a windstorm inspection for the home to stay eligible for Texas Windstorm Insurance Association coverage. See the windstorm section above.
